land.text: Aru: the east coast of Sumatra from the Deli hinterland to Asahan and Labuhan Batu, the land Iskandar Muda conquered in 1613 (the same expression the sultanate-of-aceh dossier uses); the page links Aru to Medan, Deli Serdang, Belawan, the Wampu River and the Barumun estuary

successors.note: Aru was dissolved after Iskandar Muda's 'final blow' in 1613; the sultanate-of-aceh dossier carries the gain.

land.text: Deli, founded in 1632 when Gocah Pahlawan was appointed 'to rule the former territory of Aru'

successors.note: Deli Sultanate page: a protectorate of Aceh 1632-1669, then Siak's, independent in the 1810s; a dossier for Deli is not written here.

capitals.name: Kota Rentang (Hamparan Perak)
capitals.note: Kota Rentang 'suggested as the capital'; the page gives no dated capital before the move.

capitals.name: Benteng Putri Hijau (Deli Tua)
capitals.note: 'Under Aceh pressure, the capital moved inland from Kota Rentang to Benteng Putri Hijau' in the early 16th century; the dossier takes the year after Aceh's probable capture of the port (1539).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page names no frontier: it links Aru to Medan and Deli Serdang with other proposed sites at Belawan, the Wampu River and the Barumun-Panai estuary, and says it 'controlled the northern part of the Malacca Strait'. The shape is the east-coast block Aceh conquered in 1613 (the sultanate-of-aceh dossier's gain), so the two dossiers agree. Infobox area: none.

ledger.note: 1225: the Haru kingdom is established. The infobox gives 'Established 1225'; the first dated mentions are Kublai Khan's demand of 1282 that Haru submit and its tribute to the Yuan in 1295 ('Marco Polo did not mention Aru' in 1292).

region.text: Kota Rentang (Hamparan Perak), the port city Aceh probably took in 1539

ledger.note: c. 1539: Aceh probably takes the port city of Kota Rentang. 'Probably 1539: Aceh likely took the port city of Kota Rentang' and 'under Aceh pressure' the capital moved inland to Benteng Putri Hijau; the sultanate-of-aceh dossier's 1539 gain is the Batak country, not the port, so the counterpart is read from this page alone (confidence 1).

c. 1540: the capital moves inland from Kota Rentang to Benteng Putri Hijau (Deli Tua). The page dates it to the 'early 16th century' under Aceh pressure; 1540 follows the probable loss of the port in 1539.

zones.text: Aru: the east coast of Sumatra from the Deli hinterland to Asahan and Labuhan Batu, the land Iskandar Muda conquered in 1613 (the same expression the sultanate-of-aceh dossier uses); the page links Aru to Medan, Deli Serdang, Belawan, the Wampu River and the Barumun estuary

wars.outcome: Aceh probably took Kota Rentang in 1539 and Iskandar Muda 'struck a final blow' in 1613; Aru was dissolved in the early 17th century.
wars.note: The 1564 defeat of Aru in the Ottoman expedition to Aceh is dated on the page; the Aceh dossier has no 1564 Aru event.

wars.name: Majapahit expedition to Haru and Pane
wars.outcome: 'A Majapahit naval expedition gained control of Haru and Pane' in 1339; the Nagarakretagama of 1365 lists Aru as a Majapahit vassal in Sumatra.
wars.note: No land change is drawn: the majapahit dossier carries the Sumatran lands as one vassal sphere from 1352 and should carry Aru's vassalage (1339-1365 on this page).

certainty.note: The kingdom's site is argued (Medan, Belawan, Wampu, Barumun); the shape is the land Aceh took in 1613.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Aru. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The shape is the east-coast block of the sultanate-of-aceh 1613 gain (Cliopatria's Aceh 1626 minus 1612), so there is no independent evidence of the frontier. The Aceh dossier's 1612 'Deli' gain is a separate 50 km disc on the Medan coast. The infobox 1225 is the page's; the kingdom's early history (Yuan 1282 and 1295, Majapahit 1339 and 1365) is on the page without territory. The Majapahit dossier should carry Aru as a vassal. The 'Succeeded by' field of the infobox is empty on the page. Gazetteer: Kota Rentang, Benteng Putri Hijau (Deli Tua), Hamparan Perak are not in places.jsonl.
